appraisal_events.evidence: "avec un air glacial" Charlus lectures him on two things he should learn, tells him he has had "l'air de parler à tort et à travers comme un sourd" and thereby added "un second ridicule à celui d'avoir des ancres brodées sur votre costume de bain", replaces yesterday's talk of youth's seductions with "son étourderie, ses inconséquences et son incompréhension", and dismisses him: "J'espère, monsieur, que cette petite douche ne vous sera pas moins salutaire que votre bain."
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus takes the young man's sincere protest as a pretext for a sustained icy reprimand that leaves him ridiculed and without a reply.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Sans doute eut-il regret de ces paroles": the borrowed book comes back to the narrator bound in morocco set with a cut-leather plaque "qui représentait en demi-relief une branche de myosotis".
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus withdraws from his own severity with an unspoken apology in the form of a costly gift whose forget-me-not says what he will not say, returning some ground to the narrator.

appraisal_events.evidence: At the dinner the narrator understands "que les histoires trop facilement trouvées drôles par notre camarade étaient des histoires de M. Bloch père, et que l'homme « tout à fait curieux » était toujours un de ses amis"; Bloch is placed among those one admires in childhood, "un camarade plus avancé que nous (ce que Bloch avait été pour moi)".
appraisal_events.explanation: Bloch's wit and his verdicts on people are revealed as borrowed from his father, and his old ascendancy over the narrator is filed away as a childhood illusion.

status_effects.explanation: He is comprehensively out-talked: told he answers before understanding, made ridiculous twice over, and left standing silent while Charlus closes the exchange.
He controls the whole encounter, sets its terms, delivers a polished reprimand, and ends it himself with a courteous dismissal.
The man who crushed him is shown regretting it and paying for the retraction in leather and gold, which quietly shifts some leverage back to the younger man.
The narration deflates him by tracing his best jokes and his judgments of people back to his father's stock.
